items: Shoulder: clavicle, scapula (glenoid), and humerus. The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint with a wide range of movement and is commonly dislocated.
Elbow: humerus, ulna, and radius; primarily a hinge joint.
Wrist: distal radius and carpal bones; the carpus contains eight bones.

blocks.title: Carpal bones mnemonic
blocks.text: She Looks Too Pretty, Try To Catch Her: Scaphoid, Lunate, Triquetrum, Pisiform, Trapezium, Trapezoid, Capitate, Hamate. The scaphoid is commonly fractured; anatomical snuffbox tenderness is a clinical clue.
Brachial plexus arrangement: roots C5-T1 → trunks → divisions → cords → terminal branches.

rows: Weak abduction from about 15-90 degrees; reduced sensation over the shoulder tip. May be injured in surgical-neck fracture or shoulder dislocation.
Wrist drop; may be injured with a humeral shaft fracture.
Carpal tunnel may cause paresthesia and weak thumb opposition; more proximal lesions may cause the hand-of-benediction sign on attempted fist.
Clawing of the hand and a positive Froment sign; may be injured near the medial epicondyle.

blocks.text: Subclavian → axillary → brachial → radial and ulnar arteries → palmar arches. The brachial artery is assessed in the cubital fossa; the radial artery is commonly palpated at the wrist. Allen's test can be used before radial artery puncture.

items: Anatomical snuffbox: scaphoid lies in the floor; tenderness after injury raises concern for scaphoid fracture and avascular necrosis.
Cubital fossa: important contents include the biceps tendon, brachial artery, and median nerve, arranged roughly lateral to medial; the radial nerve lies laterally.
Carpal tunnel: median nerve compression may cause night symptoms and tingling in the thumb, index, and middle fingers. Tinel and Phalen tests may support assessment.

rows: 0-15 degrees: supraspinatus; 15-90 degrees: deltoid; above 90 degrees: scapular rotation by serratus anterior and trapezius.
SITS: supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor, subscapularis.

blocks.title: Compare the common plexus injuries
items: Erb palsy (C5-C6): classic waiter-tip posture; associated with shoulder dystocia or traction on the neck.
Klumpke palsy (C8-T1): may cause claw hand; Horner syndrome can occur if sympathetic fibers are involved, classically after traction on an abducted arm.
Look for wasting, scars, deformity, or clawing.
Assess active and passive movement, including abduction and flexion/extension.
Test sensation: axillary over the regimental badge area, median at the palmar thumb, ulnar at the little finger, and radial at the dorsal first web space.
Use relevant special tests such as Tinel, Phalen, or Froment when indicated.

items.question: A patient cannot extend the wrist after a humeral shaft fracture. Which nerve is likely injured?
items.answer: The radial nerve. Assess the patient clinically and manage the injury according to local guidance; the source notes mention a cock-up splint and physiotherapy.

blocks.title: Quick nerve recall
blocks.text: Radial: wrist drop. Median: thenar weakness or ape-hand posture in selected lesions. Ulnar: clawing. Axillary: weak shoulder abduction.
